To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nuclear deformation is a significant factor in the reaction dynamics only for the reactions with the total angular momentum of about 50 MeV and higher, and that the deformation is important for the reactions with a total energy of the relative motion of 50 MeV or lower.
The shape deformation is important only if the reaction is deeply-inelastic, the time scale for shape deformation is of the order of 100-300 fm/c, and the shape deformation is not viscuous.

the shape of the nucleus is a key element in the description of the reaction mechanism and that the viscosity of the nuclear fluid plays an essential role in the description of nuclear collisions at high energies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of the nuclear equation of state and of the collective flow of nuclear matter in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.
a study of nuclear shape deformations in the process of deep inelastic collisions of heavy nuclei at energies below 1 GeV/nucleon.
the study of nuclear reactions in the energy range from 20 to 150 MeV per nucleon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nuclear deformations in heavy-ion reactions are important only for those collisions which involve nearly complete loss of relative kinetic energy.
the shape deformations in the deeply-inelastic collisions of heavy ions are of no significance for the understanding of the mechanism of these collisions.
nuclear deformations do not play a significant role in the dynamics of heavy-ion collisions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nuclear viscosity is important only in the case of deeply-inelastic heavy ion collisions.
the viscosity is important only for the reactions involving complete loss of energy.
the shape deformations of nuclei are important in deeply-inelastic collisions only when they are accompanied by a complete loss of kinetic energies of the relative motion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the shape deformation is not a major source of energy losses in heavy-ion collisions.
the viscosity in the nuclear matter is very small.
the viscosity of nuclear matter can be extracted from the analysis of the shape of the reaction product.
